City guides

WEB DESIGN across the country.

City guides for the 200 largest US metros. Each one reports our check of independent business websites in that city and what ChatGPT recommends there, with the latest Census data on who does business there, what is being built, and the state rules that shape a website. The fastest-growing metros since 2020 are Myrtle Beach (+20.9%), Lakeland (+19.8%), and Ocala (+17.3%). Compared with the same months of 2025, housing permits through August rose fastest, among these 200 metros, in Reading (+256%), Norwich (+120%), and College Station (+88%).

Everyone we work with City guides Free website check

FAQ

QUESTIONS,
answered.

Anything else? Ask us directly or email Noah at hello@endcap.design.

How much does a website cost?

We quote each project after a short conversation, once we know the pages, content, and features it needs. Your proposal lists the deliverables, schedule, and price, and we agree on it before any work begins.

How long does a website take?

Most websites take two to four weeks once the content is ready. The proposal confirms the schedule.

What kinds of businesses do you work with?

Any business that needs a website that looks right and brings in inquiries: local businesses, restaurants, professional firms, contractors, real estate companies, and software products such as My Friendly Staff, CRE Redline, and DrivewAI.

Do you work with clients outside Orange County?

Yes. Our clients so far are in Southern California, and we can work remotely with businesses in other states by video call, phone, and email. Our city guides cover local market data and state website rules for major US metros.

Who will I work with?

Noah, the founder, handles your project directly, from the first conversation through design, review, and launch.

Can you write the content?

Yes. You can supply your own text, or we write it from a conversation and your existing material. Writing is scoped in the proposal.

Will a redesign hurt our search visibility?

A redesign includes moving your existing content and redirecting each old address to its new page, so search engines and bookmarks follow the change.

What happens after launch?

Website care covers hosting, software and security updates, and up to an hour of changes each month, with no long-term contract. Larger changes are quoted before we start.

Can our domain and email stay where they are?

Yes. We can point your domain at the new website without moving your email. If you would like us to manage the domain, we set it up with your business as the owner.

How we checked

The research on each city guide

  • Which businesses Businesses with a website tag in OpenStreetMap within 10 miles of each principal city’s center: shops, restaurants, offices, trades, health, salons, fitness, hotels and similar. Chains and franchises are left out (a brand tag, or a website listed in more than one metro), as are government, schools and social-media-only links. Up to 100 per metro, in a fixed random order.
  • What we checked Each homepage was loaded and read for what a visitor and a search engine notice first: a tap-to-call link, a search description, business structured data, the copyright year, online booking or ordering, and the site builder. Sites that no longer load, and parked or placeholder domains, are counted separately; sites that block automated requests are left out.
  • Speed and accessibility Up to 30 working sites per metro, in the same order, went through Google PageSpeed Insights on a phone (October 18, 2026). Those figures are given when at least 10 sites were tested.
  • Typical metro The median of the 198 metros with at least 20 working sites. A difference is called out only when it is larger than sampling noise: 8 points for the homepage checks, 12 for the PageSpeed figures.
  • ChatGPT Three questions per metro (the best restaurants, a good dentist, a reliable plumber), asked on October 18, 2026 through OpenAI’s Codex app (gpt-5.6-luna) with web search on. Sites are the links shown in each answer, sorted into businesses’ own sites, review sites and directories, news and guides, and official sites; the businesses named were read from each answer by the same model. The Orange County pages used a different setup, so their counts are not directly comparable.
  • What we publish Counts and shares only. No business is named, and a local guide or blog is not named either; national review sites are.

Sources

  • Business counts U.S. Census Bureau, County Business Patterns 2023 (NAICS 2017) Data
  • Population U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program, Vintage 2025 Data
  • Income and housing U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year 2024 Data
  • Building permits U.S. Census Bureau, Building Permits Survey, January-August 2026 year-to-date vs. same months of 2025 Data
  • Metro definitions OMB metropolitan statistical areas, July 2023 (OMB Bulletin 23-01) Data

Figures are for the metropolitan statistical area unless noted. Business counts cover locations with paid employees. Data refreshed 2026-10-10.
